problems_fixed.what: Duplicate solution 60 within the bronze tier (also bronze[0], the 240 km in 4 h speed). Changed the liquid's density 1.2 -> 1.4 g/cm3 so mass = 1.4 x 50 = 70, a clean non-calculator answer distinct from the rest of the tier.

Pedagogically degenerate average-speed problem. With 180 km at 90 km/h (2 h) and 120 km at 60 km/h (2 h) both legs took equal time, so averaging the two speeds ALSO gives 75, making the 'do not average the speeds' misconception undetectable. Changed the second leg to 40 km/h: legs now take 2 h and 3 h, total 300 km in 5 h, average = 60 km/h, while averaging the speeds wrongly gives 65.

opener_concept: A 120-mile road trip taking 2 hours (inline SVG A-to-B journey figure). The student divides 120 by 2 in their head to get 60 mph; the reveal names it as speed = distance / time and links density (mass / volume) and pressure (force / area) as the same 'one quantity shared by another' idea.
